subject: Unexpected session merge: invoice overage and EU VAT proration
messages:
From: Alex Hsu <alex.h@brightcart.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, procurement@brightcart.com
Cc: Sophie Li <sophie.li@brightcart.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: High October bill — possible doubled sessions after SDK migration

Hi Kimberly,

We just opened our October invoice and saw a ~38% jump vs. typical month (line item: 'session tokens') — we weren't expecting that level of increase. BrightCart rolled a minor SDK change on Oct 3 that adjusted how client sessions are identified; engineering says it's possible some long-lived sessions were re-identified as new sessions after a reconnect.

Can you please: 1) provide the raw per-session usage export for Oct (by session id, start/end, token_count); 2) confirm whether Redwood's metering logic would treat those reconnects as separate billable sessions; and 3) advise on EU VAT impact if we end up issuing a credit for duplicate sessions?

I attached the invoice PDF and a short screen grab from our telemetry showing session id churn. We're on postpay monthly billing under entity BrightCart EU (VAT reg: GB999999).

Thanks — would like to get to resolution before our procurement close on Nov 30.

Best,
Alex Hsu
Head of Finance, BrightCart

Attachments: invoice_2026-10_v1.pdf (pdf), session_churn.png (image)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hsu <alex.h@brightcart.com>, procurement@brightcart.com
Cc: Sophie Li <sophie.li@brightcart.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High October bill — possible doubled sessions after SDK migration

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. We're investigating; initial notes below and next steps.

Short answer: there are two mechanisms that can produce what looks like "duplicated" sessions in billing:
- client-side session re-ids / reconnects (as you noted) where the SDK treats the reconnect as a new session id; and
- server-side TTL expiration + rewarm where an LRU/KV cache eviction causes a fresh 'cold' session that is billed separately.

What I need from you (quick):
- confirm whether the BrightCart SDK change included a client session id format change (even a small prefix) — that would cause our attribution to treat them as distinct;
- if you can share the per-session export you referenced, we will correlate against our request IDs.

What we'll do from our side:
- pull a session-level usage export for Oct by request_id/session_id and annotate suspected duplicates;
- run a de-dup check across overlapping time windows (we'll compare user agent / source IP / start/end times);
- estimate an adjustment and VAT impact for EU entity on any credit (VAT for refunds/credits is region-specific; we'll coordinate with Rafael).

I'll have a preliminary analysis plus proposed credit by EOD Monday (Nov 22). If that works, we'll also propose language for a one-time credit memo and corrected invoice.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Account Ops — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0192

Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: High October bill — possible doubled sessions after SDK migration

Team — forwarding BrightCart's ask. I have already requested the per-session export from them; attaching link to the raw usage pull (sensitive). Can you run the usual de-dup tooling and confirm root cause? Key points to validate:
- Are we seeing identical request_id clusters that map to two session_ids but the same underlying user_id/source IP?
- Is there a batch in our logs where session TTL was reduced (I recall a infra change on Oct 2 that adjusted cache TTL for the CPU-saver path)?

If duplicates are confirmed, propose the following:
1) credit BrightCart for duplicated session tokens only (do not credit genuine new sessions);
2) calculate VAT impact: because BrightCart EU is VAT-registered, the credit will reduce the taxable base — Rafael, can you confirm whether we should issue a corrected invoice with negative line item or a separate credit memo? We will need the VAT amount and ledger impact.
3) timeline: propose to send a corrected invoice + credit memo by Nov 24 to meet their procurement cutoff.

I've added this to BILL-9124 and attached the initial export link: https://drive.redwood.com/internal/brightcart/usage_oct_raw.csv

-Kim

On Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:03, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. We're investigating...

From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hsu <alex.h@brightcart.com>, Sophie Li <sophie.li@brightcart.com>, procurement@brightcart.com
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: High October bill — possible doubled sessions after SDK migration

Alex / Sophie — thanks for the patience. Summary of our analysis and proposal below.

What we found
- After correlating BrightCart's session ids against our request_id log, ~19.8% of billed "session token" volume in October mapped to clusters where the same request_id and client fingerprint appear under two different session_ids within a 10-minute window.
- The timing aligns with your SDK change on Oct 3 and an internal TTL change pushed Oct 2 (both contributed).

What we propose
1) One-time billing credit for duplicated session token volume: 19.8% of the session-token line item for October (see attached proposed-credit-memo.pdf). This is a net credit to the invoice amount that we will apply as a negative line item.
2) VAT handling: because BrightCart EU is VAT-registered, the credit reduces the taxable base. Rafael has confirmed we should issue a corrected invoice with a negative VAT line (i.e., a credit memo) rather than an informal refund — this preserves tax trail. You should see zero net VAT change if you're reclaiming VAT through your normal filings, but the corrected invoice will show the reduced net and VAT amounts.
3) Timing / paperwork: we will issue a corrected invoice + official credit memo by Nov 24. Please confirm the billing contact and the legal name for the credit memo (we have "BrightCart Europe Ltd").

Next steps for you
- Confirm legal name and VAT number to appear on the credit memo (reply-all).
- Let us know if you'd like the credit applied to Nov invoice instead of being a negative Oct adjustment (we can do either; standard is to correct the originating invoice).

Internal notes
- Credit amount estimate: $18,420 (pre-VAT) / $3,684 VAT = $22,104 gross reversal (estimate).
- Rafael to finalize VAT/legal stamp and post the corrected invoice to the ledger. Marcus will approve the credit.

Thanks — we'll get the official docs over Monday.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Ops — Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-credit-memo.pdf (pdf), invoice_2026-10_v1_adjustments.csv (csv)
